summary: Feature: Dockerize AI Service for Cloud Deployment

details.user_story: As a DevOps Engineer, I want to containerize the AI Service using Docker so that it can run reliably on Render (or any cloud provider) with all system-level dependencies pre-installed.
details.context: The AI Service relies on OpenCV (`cv2`) and MediaPipe. These libraries require system-level shared objects (like `libGL` and `libglib`) that are missing in standard 'Python Native' cloud environments. A Docker container is the only way to bundle these OS dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: A `Dockerfile` is created in the `ai-service/` directory.
The Docker build process successfully installs Python 3.12, system dependencies (`libgl1`, `libglib2.0`), and Python packages.
The `.task` model file is correctly copied into the container image.
The container exposes port 8001 and starts the FastAPI server (`uvicorn`) automatically.
Local testing (`docker run`) confirms the service responds to health checks.
technical_details: System Deps: Run `apt-get install -y libgl1-mesa-glx libglib2.0-0` before `pip install`.
Port Mapping: Ensure internal port 8001 maps correctly to the host.
edge_cases: Model File Missing: Ensure the `.dockerignore` file doesn't accidentally exclude the `.task` file.
Memory Limits: MediaPipe can be RAM hungry; ensure the container isn't immediately OOM (Out of Memory) killed on free-tier hosting.
Architecture: Ensure the image builds correctly for Linux (amd64) even if developed on Apple Silicon (arm64).
